name: Cobb
metered: At this point metered generation is net of local load, about 35% of Cobb's gross output. Where the embedded generation meter reads more, we add the difference.

about.text: Cobb stands where the Cobb River meets the Tākaka, on the edge of Kahurangi National Park in Golden Bay. Its water falls almost 600 m from the storage lake to the powerhouse, the greatest head of any power station in New Zealand, so a small flow makes a lot of power. A private company planned the scheme in the 1930s but could not raise the money; the government took it over, first power came in 1944, and a storage dam was finished in 1954. Until 1955, when a line from Stoke joined the region to the South Island grid, Cobb supplied Nelson and Tasman on its own.

facts.label: Commissioned
facts.note: first power in June 1944, as a run-of-river station; the storage dam followed in 1954

facts.label: River or lake
facts.note: the powerhouse is where the Cobb meets the Tākaka; the water comes from Cobb Reservoir, almost 600 m higher

facts.label: Owner
facts.note: The EA register's operator is still Manawa Energy Limited (Trustpower until 2022), which Contact bought on 11 July 2025.

facts.label: Previous owners
facts.value: New Zealand Government, 1940–87; Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ), 1987–99; Meridian Energy, 1999; TransAlta New Zealand, 1999–2000; NGC (Natural Gas Corporation), 2000–03; Trustpower (Manawa Energy from 2022), 2003–25
facts.note: The government took the scheme over from the Hume Pipe Company in 1940; ECNZ took over the Crown's generation on 1 April 1987; see notes for 1999–2003.

facts.label: Other ratings
facts.value: 33 MW (Contact's maximum capacity (Elenz uses the EA register's 32 MW))
